propositions: Batching N candidates into one call per ordering reduces LLM API calls from 2N to 2*ceil(N/batch), eliminating redundant system prefix transmissions and cutting input tokens by ~50% versus the pre-8415 baseline
Adding batch protocol instructions to the system prompt grows the cacheable prefix from 873 to 1337 tokens, crossing the 1024-token minimum cache threshold and enabling prefix caching

Verdict demultiplexing by candidate label rather than position ensures each candidate receives exactly one verdict, with absent or malformed entries causing only that candidate to abstain without propagating exceptions
Measured on real API calls over one query ticket and six candidates: 12 calls → 2 calls, total input_tokens 17558 → 9116 (−48.1%), with cache_write 1331 then cache_read 1331 on the batched run

Relation labels shift on 6 of 12 ordered pairs reproducibly between per-pair and batched builds, with five shifts moving conservatively away from surfacing (related_distinct→unrelated) and one unstable directional assertion that does not survive both-orderings aggregation

True positive (query's own digest as duplicate candidate) recovers identically across both builds with full confidence and same cited artifact, confirming no cross-contamination among batch neighbors on the one available ground-truth positive
